clue.text: Money invested? That's excellent!

definitions.meaning: the funds put into a business to run it
an old-fashioned British exclamation of delight, like 'splendid!'

explanation.surface: Someone cheers on hearing that their savings have been put to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is the stock of wealth put into an enterprise, and 'Capital!' is a dated British cry meaning splendid.

clue.text: Water-softener for south-west city seamen

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, in south-west England
old salts are experienced sailors

explanation.surface: A product for hard water is being marketed to sailors from a West Country port.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystals tipped into a tub soften the water and scent it, which is what this product is sold for.

clue.text: Order for French soldiers in church

parts.note: de is the French word for 'of', a common crossword use of French

indicators.note: the soldiers are placed inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British army corps

explanation.surface: An instruction is issued concerning French troops stationed in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree is an official command issued by an authority, a formal order.

clue.text: Support a chemical engineer with lumbago

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
CH is a standard abbreviation for chemical
E is an abbreviation for engineer or engineering

explanation.surface: Someone backing a chemical engineer who suffers from a bad back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbago is pain in the lower spine, the commonest kind of pain in that part of the body.

clue.text: Stops the game to serve peaches

definitions.meaning: a referee halts play by sounding his whistle
to peach is old slang for informing on someone

explanation.surface: A referee halts the match so that the fruit can be handed round.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee halts play with a blast on his whistle, and an informer who exposes wrongdoing is also said to do this.

clue.text: Dictionary in the inns of court

definitions.meaning: A well-known British dictionary publisher, beloved of crossword setters
the London legal societies where barristers have their sets of offices

explanation.surface: A dictionary is kept in the lawyers' quarters in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers practise from sets of rooms in the Inns of Court, London's legal societies, and the same name belongs to a famous dictionary.

clue.text: Silver of base quality is shining

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
low means base or inferior in quality

explanation.surface: A judgement that cheap silver nonetheless gleams.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aglow is lit up and radiant, giving off light or warmth.

clue.text: The lass moved out of top gear

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl shifts the car out of its highest gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top gear' is not the car's fastest gear but headwear: being out of it means wearing nothing on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without headwear means going bareheaded, with no covering on top.

clue.text: Injury inflicted by many a sorcerer

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
a mage is a magician or wizard

explanation.surface: A wound caused by the spell of one of many wizards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' standing for a big Roman numeral such as D is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Damage is harm or hurt done to something, much as an injury is.

clue.text: Where a meal is too readily available

definitions.meaning: food is served on a dish
an idiom for something handed over without effort

explanation.surface: Describing where dinner sits and how easily something is given away.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is served on crockery, and the idiom describes something handed over without the recipient making any effort.

clue.text: Pull out, despite being magnetic

parts.note: with can mean despite, as in 'with all his faults'
to draw is to attract, as a magnet does

explanation.surface: Someone retreats even though they have a magnetic personality.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat or remove something is to take it back or away, the same as extracting it.

clue.text: Archers show subservience to people

parts.note: to bow is to bend low in deference
men can mean people in general

explanation.surface: Bowmen bend low before ordinary folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archers' may suggest the long-running BBC radio soap The Archers, but here it simply means bow-wielders.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers shoot arrows from a bow, hence their other name.

clue.text: A lecher embraced by his favourite bird

indicators.note: the first pieces are held inside the word for a favourite, as in an embrace

parts.note: a pet is a favourite person or animal
a rake is a dissolute womaniser

explanation.surface: A dirty old man is hugged by his beloved budgie.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small long-tailed parrot, a kind of bird.

clue.text: Difficult customer demands solid piece of luggage

parts.note: hard means firm and solid
a case is a suitcase

explanation.surface: An awkward client insists on a rigid suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, hard-bitten person who is not easily dealt with is called this.

clue.text: Warned that education needs restructuring

indicators.note: the word education is broken apart and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A warning has been given that the school system must be reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: To caution someone is to give them a warning, so cautioned is the past form.

clue.text: To make summaries is not practical

definitions.meaning: to precis a paper or article

explanation.surface: Writing digests is said to be no practical use.
explanation.definitionFit: Summarising a paper is to precis it, and an idea that is theoretical rather than concrete is called this too.

clue.text: Shooter mad to play the fiddle

parts.note: cross means angry, mad
to bow is to draw a bow across violin strings

explanation.surface: A gunman is angry at having to perform on the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: This medieval weapon fires bolts, so it is a kind of shooter.

clue.text: Dash across, only to get knocked down

explanation.surface: Someone sprints over the road and is promptly hit by a car.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurry over somewhere is to nip across it, and a pedestrian struck by a car is said to be this.

clue.text: It may see many set free

definitions.text: It may see many set free

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are freed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pardon that releases a large number of prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: An official pardon for a group, typically releasing many prisoners at once.

clue.text: None too soon for fun

explanation.surface: It is overdue for some enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue is about to happen at last, and a lively, enjoyable spell is also called this.

clue.text: By the sound of it, go for the rodent

indicators.note: the words go for are to be heard rather than read

parts.note: the phrase spoken as said

explanation.surface: Attack the burrowing animal, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrowing North American animal related to squirrels, so a kind of rodent.

clue.text: Really popular with footballers going to court

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the FA is the Football Association

explanation.surface: Truly in favour with soccer players heading to a tribunal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is actually true is like saying it is genuinely so.

clue.text: A bishop going to an island in Scotland

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman travels to a Scottish isle.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is a large island in the Firth of Clyde off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Guessed sailor came in drunk

indicators.note: the sailor enters the word for drunk, ending up inside it

parts.note: supped means drank, consumed
OS is an ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: Someone surmised the seaman had arrived home intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or conjecture, so guessed fits the past form.

clue.text: Accountants in public appear gloomy

indicators.note: the accountants are placed inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
CAs are chartered accountants

explanation.surface: Bookkeepers look miserable when seen in public.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is clouded over, dull and dark.

clue.text: They happen to be memorable occasions

explanation.surface: Things that occur turn out to be notable days.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurrences are things that take place, and special or notable occasions are also called this.

clue.text: Not the star of "my fair lady"?

definitions.text: Not the star of "my fair lady"?

parts.words: Not the star of "my fair lady"?
parts.note: read 'fair' as light-haired: a woman who is not fair-haired would never be cast in the title role

explanation.surface: Someone who was not the lead in the famous musical.
explanation.walkthrough: My Fair Lady is the musical, but 'fair' here means blonde, so the woman is one with dark hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman with dark hair is the opposite of a fair-haired lady.
